Anna — thanks for the note and the sample invoice. High-level checklist below (short version for your procurement/legal):

- Required vendor evidence for EU suppliers:
  - Official company registration (local extract) OR VAT registration certificate (VAT ID shown)
  - Tax residency declaration if invoicing from a different jurisdiction
  - Bank account details (IBAN + BIC) and legal entity name matching the invoice
  - If applicable: EORI can be provided as supplemental metadata but does not replace VAT ID for tax reclaim/reverse-charge validation

- Invoice requirements for Redwood PO processing (must include):
  - Redwood PO Number (format: RW-<6 digits>) in a dedicated ‘PO’ field
  - Supplier VAT ID (EU VAT number) and supplier legal name
  - Invoice line items with gross amounts and a separate tax line (or a reverse-charge statement)
  - Invoice date and unique invoice number
  - If reverse-charge applies: include phrase ‘Reverse charge (Art. 196 VAT Directive) — VAT to be accounted for by the customer’ or local language equivalent

- Consolidated invoicing: acceptable for recurring/low-value POs if: (1) each consolidated invoice references the individual PO numbers it covers, and (2) the total per consolidated invoice does not exceed agreed credit term limits. We can accept monthly consolidations for amounts under €10k provided you list individual POs.

Next steps: please complete the attached Redwood vendor onboarding form (DocuSign link below) and upload the VAT certificate and company extract. I’ve copied Laura from Finance for the PO-billing entity mapping.

DocuSign (vendor form): https://docusign.com/tx/abc123-vendor-form
HubSpot deal: https://app.redwood.com/hubspot/deals/DEAL-8842

If you prefer, we can schedule a 20-minute screen share to walk through the invoice sample mapping.

3) We don’t currently include EORI on our standard invoice template — if it’s only supplemental, we can add it in the invoice footer.

I’ve attached the sample invoice again with highlights where we would place the reverse charge line.

Laura / Karthik — forwarding GlobalPack’s questions. Quick summary and asks:

- UK branch invoices: we can accept UK VAT registration for invoice validation provided the billing legal entity on the invoice matches the bank account and the supplier registration we store (i.e., the UK entity must be the one on the vendor record).
- Wording: finance prefers two accepted templates depending on jurisdiction:
  - EU (B2B reverse charge): ‘Reverse charge — VAT to be accounted for by the recipient (Art. 196 Directive).’
  - UK (post-Brexit services): ‘Reverse charge — VAT to be accounted for by the recipient under UK VAT domestic reverse charge rules.’

Action items: can Finance confirm acceptance of UK VAT IDs for Q1 billing and whether we need an additional tax residency attestation for the UK branch? Also, Karthik — legal/tax, any preference on canonical wording or a required domestic reference we should provide to vendors?

I’ve attached the completed vendor onboarding form (pending signature) and GlobalPack’s sample invoice.

Thanks,
Marissa

Marissa / Anna — thanks for the clear thread. Confirming from Finance + AP:

- UK branch invoices: accepted. We require:
  1) Invoice issuer name exactly matching the vendor record legal name in our system.
  2) Bank account country and IBAN that corresponds to the billing legal entity.
  3) Supplier VAT/Tax ID for the issuing country.

- Wording (confirmed): please use the UK wording Marissa suggested for any invoices issued by the UK branch. For EU invoices where reverse-charge applies, use the EU wording listed. We recommend vendors put the reverse charge line directly under the net/amount breakdown so our automated parser picks it up.

- Consolidated invoices: accepted for monthly consolidation. Requirement: consolidated invoice must include a table mapping each invoice line to the Redwood PO (RW-######). If GlobalPack prefers, we can accept a CSV that lists PO -> invoice line mappings attached to the consolidated invoice.

Next steps for GlobalPack:
  1) Sign the DocuSign vendor onboarding form (Marissa, I see the pending link).
  2) Upload VAT certificate and company extract to the DocuSign upload or send to procurement@redwood.com.
  3) Once the vendor record is created we will issue the first Redwood PO (format RW-123456).

Anna — if you send a test invoice (PDF) with the exact UK/EU wording and the PO number placeholder, Finance will run it through the parser and confirm success within 24 working hours.
